facts.statement: Almadasuchus is an extinct crocodylomorph found in the early Late Jurassic Puesto Almada Member of the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Almadasuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorph known from the early Late Jurassic (early Oxfordian stage) Puesto Almada Member of the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation of Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Almadasuchus contains only one known species, Almadasuchus figarii.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Almadasuchus figarii.

facts.statement: The species is known from holotype MPEF-PV 3838, which includes a well-preserved posterior skull region and additional skull and postcranial bones.
facts.quote: It is known from the holotype MPEF-PV 3838, a well-preserved posterior region of the skull as well as other skull and postcranial remains.

facts.statement: The quadrate of Almadasuchus connects to the basisphenoid and exoccipital bones, which likely made its skull completely akinetic (immovable).
facts.quote: The quadrate of Almadasuchus is not completely fused to the braincase, but makes connections with two braincase bones, the basisphenoid and the exoccipital. These two attachment points probably made the skull of Almadasuchus completely akinetic.

facts.statement: Almadasuchus lived during the Oxfordian stage, approximately 161.5 to 159 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 159 million years ago)

facts.statement: Almadasuchus belongs to the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
The genus Almadasuchus was described by Pol et al. in 2013.
The species Almadasuchus figarii was named by Pol et al. in 2013.
